text:
anna: deploy-bot just put release/4578 on hold for an SBOM provenance flag. canary hit 8% before the gate. change window is 2h. do we pin the transitive dep or rollback the release? cc @samir @maria @jen :eyes:

deploy-bot: RELEASE_HOLD - SBOM_PROVENANCE_UNVERIFIED detected for package fasthash@^1.2.0 (transitive). Evidence: https://ci.redwood/internal/sbom/4578 - hold initiated by policy 'provenance-strict' :rotating_light:

samir: thanks. quick Q — is fasthash actually in the runtime path for the model server, or only in a buildtool used during image build?

anna: it's a build-only transitive brought in by image-builder -> helper-lib -> fasthash. runtime tree doesn't import it. the binary image was built from base-image v2.3.1 which we pinned last month.

lee: if it's build-only, security-wise provenance still matters for compliance, but the risk to runtime is low. we can either pin the image digest to the verified base (if available) or rebuild with a patched builder image. rebuild will take ~30-45m.

maria: canary is at 8% and healthy aside from the gate. my preference is to avoid a rollback if customers aren't impacted. options:
- quick pin: update image reference to base-image@sha256:<digest> and push a new release (fast, low risk)
- rebuild: produce a new image from a vetted builder (takes time)
- rollback: revert to previous release 4567 (fast but loses the feature)

anna: pin or rebuild both OK. if we pin, we need a security exception record unless we can attach provenance evidence to the pinned digest.

compliance-bot: Exception required if SBOM provenance cannot be verified for transitive dependencies. Exception workflow: create ticket in GRC queue with justification, attach SBOM snapshot and risk assessment. Approval needed from Security Lead within 8 business hours.

jen: for release notes — if we pin and keep the rollout, we should add a note: "Rolled out with base-image pinned to verified digest due to SBOM provenance verification step." keep it minimal.

samir: propose this plan: 1) try quick pin to base-image@sha256:abcd1234 (we have that digest in the artifact registry). 2) restart canary with pinned image. 3) open GRC exception ticket with SBOM evidence and notify security for approval. 4) if security denies, rollback to 4567. Anyone object?

anna: +1. I'll kick off the pin and canary restart. posting the exact commands in case someone needs to reproduce:

```
# pin base image
gcloud artifacts docker images add-tag us-central1-docker.pkg/redwood/base-image:v2.3.1 us-central1-docker.pkg/redwood/base-image@sha256:abcd1234
# restart canary
deployctl rollout restart release/4578 --image us-central1-docker.pkg/redwood/base-image@sha256:abcd1234 --strategy canary
```

lee: sounds good. also add a short alert rule to watch 5xx and latency for the canary group for the next 4 hours. maria can you handle that?

maria: on it. will create a temporary alert and a dashboard slice for the canary.

compliance-bot: Note: if the exception is approved, record the approval ID in the release notes and the GRC ticket.

deploy-bot: action accepted: pin applied. canary restarted at 2678901302 with image digest sha256:abcd1234. Monitoring hooks attached.

anna: thanks all. tracking: PR #7890 (image pin), GRC-10234 (exception ticket). I'll update release notes and keep this thread synced.

samir: decision summary for the log: pinned base-image digest to satisfy SBOM gate, canary resumed, security exception opened. fallback = rollback to 4567 if security rejects or canary shows regression.

jen: adding release note blurb and a devex blurb for the changelog: "Hotfix: pinned base image digest due to SBOM provenance validation; no runtime behavior changes."

maria: canary metrics look normal at 30m. no spikes. keeping alerts for 4h.

anna: closing this thread once security approves or we perform rollback. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
